clauses.label: S ection  1.
clauses.text:
S ection  1. There is hereby established a Defense Distinguished  
Service Medal, with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for  
award by the Secretary of Defense to a military officer who performed  
exceptionally meritorious service in a duty of great responsibility with  
the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Organization of the Joint  
Chiefs of Staff, a specified or unified command, a Defense agency, or  
such other joint activity as may be designated by the Secretary of  
Defense.

clauses.label: S ec. 2.
clauses.text:
S ec. 2. The Defense Distinguished Service Medal and appurtenances  
thereto shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary  
of Defense and shall be awarded under such regulations as he shall  
prescribe. These regulations shall place the Defense Distinguished  
Service Medal in an order of precedence after the Medals of Honor  
and the Distinguished Service Crosses of the Armed Forces and before  
the Distinguished Service Medals of the Armed Forces.

clauses.label: S ec. 3.
clauses.text:
S ec. 3. No more than one Defense Distinguished Service Medal  
shall be awarded to any one person, but for each succeeding exception­
ally meritorious period of service justifying such an award, a suitable  
device may be awarded to be worn witn that Medal as prescribed by  
appropriate regulations of the Department of Defense.

clauses.label: S ec. 4.
clauses.text:
S ec. 4. The Defense Distinguished Service Medal or device ma^be  
awarded posthumously and, when so  
such representative of the deceased as  
the Secretary of Defense.

Executive Order 11545
ESTABLISHING THE DEFENSE DISTINGUTSHED SERVICE MEDAL
By virtue of the authority Vested in' me as President of the United  
States and as Commander in Chief of the Armed Forces of the United  
States, it is ordered as follows:
S ection  1. There is hereby established a Defense Distinguished  
Service Medal, with accompanying ribbons and appurtenances, for  
award by the Secretary of Defense to a military officer who performed  
exceptionally meritorious service in a duty of great responsibility with  
the Office of the Secretary of Defense, the Organization of the Joint  
Chiefs of Staff, a specified or unified command, a Defense agency, or  
such other joint activity as may be designated by the Secretary of  
Defense.
S ec. 2. The Defense Distinguished Service Medal and appurtenances  
thereto shall be of appropriate design approved by the Secretary  
of Defense and shall be awarded under such regulations as he shall  
prescribe. These regulations shall place the Defense Distinguished  
Service Medal in an order of precedence after the Medals of Honor  
and the Distinguished Service Crosses of the Armed Forces and before  
the Distinguished Service Medals of the Armed Forces.
S ec. 3. No more than one Defense Distinguished Service Medal  
shall be awarded to any one person, but for each succeeding exception­
ally meritorious period of service justifying such an award, a suitable  
device may be awarded to be worn witn that Medal as prescribed by  
appropriate regulations of the Department of Defense.
S ec. 4. The Defense Distinguished Service Medal or device ma^be  
awarded posthumously and, when so  
such representative of the deceased as  
the Secretary of Defense.
T h e W hite  H ouse ,
July 9,1970.
[F.R. Doc. 70-8935; Filed, July 9, 1970; 3:08 p.m.]

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11545 (signed July 9, 1970; 35 FR 11161, Federal Register issue of July 11, 1970) establishes the Defense Distinguished Service Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text (a machine text layer of the printed page): an authority paragraph and four sections (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and precedence; one medal with devices; posthumous award). The held text has a few dropped words in section 4 and a misspelled title, so I quote nothing from those lines. The dossier inventory is one clause covering the whole order and I confirmed it without correction. The order has no end date or ending condition and revokes nothing. EO 14085 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541), section 6, amends it: section 1 is amended by striking military officer and inserting member of the Armed Forces of the United States, and section 2 by striking he and inserting the Secretary. That is a later event on a continuing clause, recorded with its text before and after in the clause reason, not an end. The held-text number search also finds only the 1989 OFR codification snapshot (historical editorial, not a current basis) and EO 14085. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 1125 with no ending statement (a machine pointer; held statutory text is not relied on). The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record only the EO 14085 amendment and no revocation or supersession. The clause is operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
